solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Crack that would be issue beneath base

indicators.note: the clue says the remainder is what sits beneath the base letter in the word for issue, so that letter is taken off the top

parts.note: to issue troops with kit is to equip them
e is the base of natural logarithms in maths

explanation.surface: A wisecrack about some matter being beneath someone's dignity.
explanation.walkthrough: Read it as a riddle: the answer is what would make 'issue' if it stood beneath 'base', e, the mathematical constant. So take E off the front of EQUIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack is a witty remark, the same as a joke or wisecrack.

clue.text: Small length of machine's lead caught in appliance

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its front letter, so only the start of machine's is used
the letter for caught is placed in the word for appliance

parts.note: an iron is a household appliance
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A tiny measurement of a machine part gets snagged inside a household gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A micron is a millionth of a metre, a very small unit of length.

clue.text: Rebellious group's concerning opinion about current head of state

parts.note: re means concerning, as in business letters

indicators.note: the word for opinion goes around the pair of letters that follow

parts.note: a stance is a position or opinion
I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so state gives its initial

explanation.surface: A rebel faction's view of the country's leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A resistance is an underground movement fighting an occupier, so a rebellious group.

clue.text: Coolness from a doctor holding device endlessly

indicators.note: the A and doctor letters hold the shortened device between them

parts.note: MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine

indicators.note: endlessly means the word for device loses its final letter

parts.note: a ploy is a scheme or device

explanation.surface: A calm doctor keeps hold of some gadget that has no end.
explanation.definitionFit: Aplomb is self-possession under pressure, the same as coolness or composure.

clue.text: Resent new girl oddly ignored in shift

indicators.note: the kept letters go in the word for shift

parts.note: to budge is to shift or move

indicators.note: the odd letters of new girl are dropped, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: Someone resents a new girl being ignored during a work shift.
explanation.definitionFit: To begrudge is to resent or envy someone what they have.

clue.text: One serving a drink

parts.note: a colonel, Col, is one serving in the army

explanation.surface: A waiter or barman serving someone a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One serving' looks like a waiter, but it is a serving officer, a colonel.
explanation.definitionFit: Cola is a fizzy soft drink flavoured with kola nut.

clue.text: Bones from male evil adult concealed in sack

indicators.note: the letters for evil and adult are hidden inside the word for sack

parts.note: to sack is to fire, or axe, someone
ill means evil, as in ill deeds
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: Bones of a wicked grown man hidden in a sack, a murder story.
explanation.definitionFit: Maxillae are the upper jawbones, plural of maxilla.

clue.text: Wow, angry eccentric completely flipped, perhaps

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so these letters are put out of order

parts.note: up means completely, as in eaten up or used up

explanation.surface: An exclamation at someone furious and odd who has totally lost it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipped' looks like losing one's temper, matching 'angry'; here it means turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flipped over ends upside down, inverted; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.

clue.text: No good sacking leader to be profitable

indicators.note: sacking the leader means dismissing the first letter

parts.note: futile means useless, no good

explanation.surface: A business saying it is no good firing the boss if you want to make money.
explanation.definitionFit: Utile is a rare word for useful or advantageous, hence profitable.

clue.text: Botched up art containing winged deity that once flew

indicators.note: the jumbled letters contain the god's name
botched means made a mess of, so the letters of up art are jumbled

parts.note: Eros is the winged Greek god of love

explanation.surface: A messed-up painting of a winged god, from a time it was popular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Botched' makes PTAUR from UP ART, which goes around EROS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pterosaurs were flying reptiles of the dinosaur age, now extinct, so creatures that flew long ago.

clue.text: Left in charge of building construction

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
o' is a shortened of, as in man o' war

explanation.surface: Someone left in charge of a building project.
explanation.definitionFit: A portico is a roofed porch with columns at a building's entrance, an architectural structure.

clue.text: Set straight a learner breaking rule

indicators.note: the A and L break into the word for rule

parts.note: to reign is to rule
L is the learner-driver plate letter

explanation.surface: A trainee breaks a rule and is put right.
explanation.definitionFit: To realign something is to bring it back into line, making it straight again.

clue.text: Fill big belly with popular drink

indicators.note: fill tells us the belly word is stuffed with the popular word

parts.note: a pot or pot belly is a big belly
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: Stuffing a beer gut with a favourite tipple.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinot is a grape variety and the wine made from it, such as pinot noir.

clue.text: Bread in French stick must be superior to Republican — one's fussy

indicators.note: in a down clue, superior means above, so the stick comes on top of the R

parts.note: pain is French for bread
a stake is a pointed stick

explanation.surface: A baguette insisting it is better than an American politician, a fussy type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French stick' suggests a baguette; it splits into 'in French' and 'stick'.
explanation.definitionFit: A painstaker is a person who takes pains, being meticulous and particular.

clue.text: Colleague unworthy of covering government department left

indicators.note: the word for unworthy of covers the department and left letters

parts.note: below someone, like beneath them, means unworthy of them
DfE is the UK Department for Education

explanation.surface: A workmate too lowly to cover for a government office that has been abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedfellows are associates or allies, as in strange bedfellows, so colleagues.

clue.text: Fraudulently tape cinema release

indicators.note: done fraudulently, the letters of tape cinema are faked into a new order

explanation.surface: Illegally recording a film being shown at the pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'release' looks like a film release, but it is a verb meaning set free.
explanation.definitionFit: To emancipate is to set free from bondage or restriction.

clue.text: Without concern, angrily imprisoning knight with Spanish page

indicators.note: the angry word locks the other pieces inside it

parts.note: irate means angry, so irately is angrily
N is the chess notation for knight
con is Spanish for with
a side is a page of writing

explanation.surface: Someone furiously locks up a knight and his Spanish attendant, with no thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'page' looks like a young attendant to the knight; it is a side of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting thoughtlessly toward others' feelings, showing no regard for them.

clue.text: Furniture around entrance of rancid squats

indicators.note: the furniture word goes around that letter

parts.note: couches are items of furniture

indicators.note: the entrance of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Sofas placed round the doorway of foul squatted houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squats' looks like occupied buildings; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To squat is to bend low on one's haunches, as one who stoops down does.

clue.text: Absurdities from rant about leaving dictionaries in a mess

indicators.note: the letters of rant are to be taken out, leaving the rest
in a mess means the remaining letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tirade about books of words being left untidy.
explanation.walkthrough: Take R, A, N, T from DICTIONARIES and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiocies are foolish acts or remarks, things that are absurd.

clue.text: Cut queue? That could be a result

parts.note: to score is to cut a mark into something
a line is a queue

explanation.surface: Pushing into a queue: could that pay off?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut queue' suggests jumping the line; it splits into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoreline is a final match score, like two-nil, the outcome of a game.

clue.text: Space no longer available after one's replaced old machinery

parts.note: an en is a printer's space

indicators.note: replaced means one letter takes another's place

parts.note: gone means no longer available
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A slot that's gone once an old machine has been swapped out.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine is a machine that turns energy into motion, so a piece of machinery.

clue.text: Beginning to crave lighter device to hold

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a lamp is a lighter, something that lights

explanation.surface: Starting to long for a cigarette lighter to grip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lighter' looks like a cigarette lighter; it is a light source.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamp is a tool for gripping things firmly together.

clue.text: Ancient European invading or supporting area

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means below, so the gold word comes under the area letter
the European letter invades the combined area and gold letters

parts.note: or is the heraldic name for gold

explanation.surface: An old European invading or backing a region, a history lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' looks like a link; it is gold in heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has existed for ages, very old.

clue.text: Old bit of Circle Line unused in frozen rain and cold

parts.note: an arc is part of a circle's circumference

indicators.note: unused means the line letter is left out

parts.note: hail is frozen rain
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: An old stretch of London's Circle Line out of use in sleet and cold.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route; here it splits into 'Circle' and 'Line'.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic means belonging to an earlier period, old-fashioned.

clue.text: Ship from Volgograd returned

indicators.note: returned means those letters are read backwards
from indicates the letters are taken from within the city name

explanation.surface: A vessel coming back from the Russian city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth.

clue.text: Creatures shot, pelts picked up

parts.note: a shot is a go, an attempt

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word sounds the same

parts.note: pelts are animal skins, or furs

explanation.surface: Animals that have been shot and skinned, their hides gathered up.
explanation.definitionFit: Gophers are burrowing rodents of North America, small animals.

clue.text: Legume very ably cored and served up

parts.note: so means very, as in so good

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the letters are sent upwards, read backwards
cored means the middle is removed, leaving the outside letters

explanation.surface: A bean that's skilfully cored and dished up.
explanation.definitionFit: Soya is a bean, the soybean, a member of the pea family.

clue.text: Plant eastern bank over river before erosion at the sides

indicators.note: before places the river letter ahead of the next piece
the bank word lies over the river letter, straddling it as a bridge would

parts.note: a verge is a grassy bank by a road

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its outer letters

explanation.surface: Vegetation on a riverbank, eroding at the edges.
explanation.definitionFit: An evergreen is a tree or shrub that keeps its leaves all year.

clue.text: Box 19 having article inside swapped with second in 14

indicators.note: swapped with means one letter is exchanged for another

parts.note: the answer to 19 is a scoreline, a tally
a is the indefinite article
the second letter of the answer at 14 is E

explanation.surface: A cross-referencing clue with no picture of its own.
explanation.walkthrough: TALLY contains the article A; swap it for the E that is second in 14.
explanation.definitionFit: Box is British slang for television, as is telly.
